"eight equilateral triangles" alone occurs over 500 times in Dolma.

notes: Stored edit (very_unlikely): 'a Platonic solid composed of eight equilateral triangles' is the regular octahedron's standard description (Dolma: 'eight equilateral triangles' 528). The regular octahedron is treated as an individual solid, as the topic's other Platonic-solid facts are (dual_of, number_of); the edit moves its faces from the class equilateral triangle to the class square. Chosen for coverage (CRITERIA Rule 12): the new relation has_face_shape carries the role chain has_face_shape ∘ subclass_of ⊑ has_face_shape (two chain queries, one through two subclass steps), and a fact about the faces' new class gives two composition queries (angle, diagonals; justify.py 2026-10-31: the route is has_face_shape plus a fact about the shape, not a class rule, so they are composition rather than inheritance). All four discriminate. Mathematics leaves out worlds (README, Shape per topic): a fact about a number or a shape rests on definitions and proofs, so the edit leaves no consistent world to split between. Derived queries ask what the edit forces through the definitions, holding the definitions fixed; a model that still gives the old answer holds the edit only as a patch. The edit is geometrically impossible (squares cannot close up into an eight-faced regular solid, and the face, edge and vertex counts no longer fit Euler's formula); the README allows an edit across a boundary, and no derived query asks the counts. Near: the icosahedron's faces share the relation; reference 'an equilateral triangle' differs from the new answer 'a square' (Rule 7). R2: 'octahedron' names eight faces, not their shape; 正八面体 likewise.
